summary: A first-person reflection on how a neighborhood's policing and safety changed after Mayor Thomas Hendricks and Police Chief Lisa Radcliffe launched a community policing plan in September 2023. The note covers a beat cop, town hall meetings, social worker partnerships, new technology, a youth mentorship program, and record-low crime by June 2024. It closes on ongoing challenges and a planned reintegration program for formerly incarcerated people.
one_line: A resident recounts how community policing, social workers, technology and youth mentorship cut crime to record lows in their neighborhood from 2023 to 2024.
key_facts: Mayor Thomas Hendricks and new Police Chief Lisa Radcliffe unveiled a comprehensive community safety plan in September 2023.
Officer James Keller is the newly appointed beat cop, who mingles with residents, attends community events and aims to be a familiar face rather than just a figure of authority.

By mid-October 2023, town hall meetings brought together community leaders, police officers and residents, including retired school teacher Mrs. Sylvia Watson and young entrepreneur Rodrigo Velez, to discuss neighborhood watch programs and youth engagement.
Officers are paired with social workers such as Sarah Bennett to handle mental health and domestic dispute calls with care rather than force.
As 2023 drew to a close, Chief Radcliffe rolled out dashboard cameras and bodycams as standard issue and an app for residents to report incidents, with anonymity if desired.
The control room was renamed the Community Safety Hub and operates as an open facility.
By early 2024, metrics such as response times, resolution rates and community satisfaction had significantly improved, and feedback loops fed into policy, training and daily operations.

The Future Protectors Program, launched in March 2024, mentors youth and bridges the gap between teenagers and law enforcement; Ava Jackson and Miguel Gonzales helped shape its workshops and outreach.
Crime statistics in June 2024 fell to a record low for the community.
The Annual Community Policing Forum and continual strategy reviews are meant to sustain the momentum.
A 'one size fits all' approach was discarded in favor of policies tailored to different neighborhoods, and budget and resource allocation discussions were among the challenges.
The community is about to add an integration program for recently reformed individuals to rejoin society.
